patterns.message: Import from '@/lib/booking' instead. A feature's internals are private — that is what stops a change inside booking breaking services. See ARCHITECTURE.md.

Import from '@/lib/payments' (server) or '@/lib/payments/client' (isomorphic). The gateway adapters are private — a caller that reaches esewa.ts directly is a second place that knows which gateway is in play, and importing the server entry from a Client Component fails the build on node:crypto. See ARCHITECTURE.md.
Import from '@/lib/auth' (isomorphic), '@/lib/auth/session' (server) or '@/lib/auth/otp' (client). Everything else under lib/auth is private. See ARCHITECTURE.md.

Import from '@/lib/verification'. Match keys only work if every one of them was built the same way — a caller that reaches match-keys.ts directly is a second place that knows how, and the day the fold changes the two stop agreeing. See ARCHITECTURE.md.
Import Link from '@/i18n/navigation'. One stray next/link drops a Nepali reader back into English and nothing fails.

Import from '@/lib/sms'. Which gateway is in play is one decision made in one place — a caller that reaches sparrow.ts directly is a second, and switching provider stops being one variable. See ARCHITECTURE.md.

Import from '@/lib/provider'. The rate clamp and the availability decay are single decisions — a second caller reaching past the entry is a second place that can disagree about what a professional may charge or how long 'available now' lasts. See ARCHITECTURE.md.

paths.name: next/navigation
paths.message: Import redirect, useRouter and usePathname from '@/i18n/navigation' — the next/navigation versions drop the locale. notFound and useSearchParams are fine from here.
